**Order filled:** 23 shares of MSFT at $420.50 = **$9,671.50** (within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily limits; no cash moved out of the account).

**Summary:** I read Microsoft's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, filed July 30, 2024) and decided to buy. Microsoft reported **total revenue of $245.1 billion (exactly $245,122 million), up 16% from $211,915 million**, driven by growth in every segment — Intelligent Cloud revenue rose 20% to $105.4 billion on 30% Azure growth, Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $137.4 billion (+23%), and Gaming grew 39% including the Activision Blizzard acquisition. Profitability and cash generation were equally solid: **operating income of $109,433 million (+24%)**, **net income of $88,136 million (+22%)**, **diluted EPS of $11.80 (+22%)**, and **operating cash flow of $118,548 million**, alongside a strong balance sheet ($75.5 billion in cash and short-term investments). With the stock quoting at $420.18 (bid $420.16 / ask $420.20), I placed a single limit buy order for 23 shares at $420.50 — just above the ask to be "close to market" while staying under the $10,000 cap (24 shares would have exceeded it at ~$10,085) — and it filled at $420.50 for a total of $9,671.50. No sales were made and no funds were withdrawn.
